excerpt: Lime rents shared e-scooters and e-bikes by the minute in about 230 cities across 29 countries. Founded in 2017 and backed by Uber, it listed on Nasdaq (LIME) in July 2026 after pricing its IPO at $25 a share.
content:
Lime runs shared electric scooters and electric bikes that people unlock with a phone app and ride for short trips around a city, paying for the time they use. Riders find a vehicle on the app's map, scan it to unlock, ride, and park where the city allows. Lime's vehicles can also be booked through the Uber app; that channel made up 14.3% of Lime's 2025 revenue, according to its IPO filing. Renaissance Capital, summarising Lime's IPO prospectus, reported that Lime describes itself as the largest global shared micromobility business, operating in about 230 cities across 29 countries at the end of 2025 and serving about 19 million riders that year, with roughly 27% market share across the countries it operates in and 37% in the US.

Lime was founded in 2017 and is based in San Francisco; its legal entity is Neutron Holdings. The Next Web reported that co-founder Brad Bao, chief executive Wayne Ting and president Joseph Kraus sold shares in the IPO. Uber owns more than 10% of Lime and guarantees some of its debt, The Next Web reported.

Public since July 2026. Lime filed for a Nasdaq listing in May 2026. Its prospectus showed revenue of $886.7 million in 2025, up 29%, and a net loss of $59.3 million. On 30 June 2026 it priced its IPO at $25 a share, the midpoint of its range, raising about $174 million, and began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker LIME on 1 July, Renaissance Capital and The Next Web reported. Uber had indicated interest in buying up to $20 million of shares in the offering.

Ride prices vary by city and are shown in the Lime app before you unlock. Lime's website blocked our checks, so we do not quote prices. This profile draws on published reporting and IPO coverage. We have not tested the service, and nothing here is paid placement or investment advice.

faq.a: Yes. It priced its IPO at $25 a share on 30 June 2026 and began trading on Nasdaq as LIME on 1 July 2026.

faq.q: How many cities is Lime in?
faq.a: About 230 cities across 29 countries at the end of 2025, according to its prospectus as summarised by Renaissance Capital.
Not on a net-income basis: its 2025 net loss was $59.3 million on revenue of $886.7 million.

faq.q: How much does a Lime ride cost?
faq.a: It depends on the city; the app shows the price before you unlock.
